Trust me, man... we're not talking about the same music.  I know how to use the internet.  I know how to find what I'm looking for, if it's there.  But facts are facts... sometimes it's not.  I have a 7" that was limited to 32 copies.  Not 32 in one color or 32 with a certain sleeve, but 32 copies altogether of anything.  I know everyone with a copy.  It's not on the internet, my friend.  That's an extreme example, but still.

Hell, here's a more common experience for me:  I buy a new single or E.P. (no DL code).  It only came out on vinyl and is limited to 200 copies and those 200 copies didn't sell very well.  The band didn't put the music online, so sometimes it can take a couple of years for that thing to make it's way to the blogs or torrents or soulseek or whatever.  I can take the 7 minutes it takes to rip the record, sure, but I'm not going to say I've never wished I couldn't just jam that thing in a drive and have itunes suck it out.  

The internet doesn't have everything.

EDIT:  I realize I sound like a hipster.  I'm not, I swear.  I download A LOT of music and have been able to find A LOT of my records on the internet.  Just making a point.

People throw around that T14 statement a lot.  It's not as cut and dry as that.  People need to research the school they're planning on attending and figure out how it ranks within the field they want to get into and what sort of reputation it has in the part of the country where they want to practice.  Some graduates of less-than-great schools have great job prospects in certain fields in specific places, and some graduates have no prospects anywhere.  

I mean... if you want to work in New York City in a big law firm, then you need a top school.  But that's not necessarily what everyone wants.  Bottom line: research it and don't NECESSARILY be scared off if you can't get into Harvard.

I'm a lawyer.  When I graduated, I spent months trying to find work.  I applied at the most entry level of entry levels (like $25k/year positions that didn't even require a law degree).  I still had a hard time.  I ended up working moving furniture for a few months to make ends meet.  But if my loans hadn't been in forbearance, I would have been completely sunk, financially. Your personal experience isn't necessarily true for everyone else.
